text:
Alana (Finance): Heads-up: Procurely sent the renewal quote for their embedding store. pricing looks higher than last year. link: https://procurely.com/quote/renewal-2024
Rahul (Procurement): I pulled the quote into the vendor spreadsheet. spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/sheets/d/1Xprocurely-eval
Priya (ML): Can you paste the key numbers? curious about egress and per-index costs.
Alana (Finance): Sure, pasted below from their PDF (rounded):
```
Base fee: $18,000/month
Storage: $0.045 / GB / month
Read ops: $0.0025 / 1k
Write ops: $0.01 / 1k
Egress: $0.09 / GB
99.9% SLA included
```
Rahul (Procurement): Compared to last year we were at $12k base, storage $0.03/GB, egress $0.06/GB. That's a ~50% lift on base and +50% on egress.
Priya (ML): That egress hurt — our eval pipelines pull full vectors for similarity search during reindexing. Could be significant. Can we push them on egress caps or lower tiers?
Sam @Procurely: Hi all — happy to help. We do offer "developer" tiers that match last year's rates but they cap QPS and remove dedicated shards. We can also do negotiated bundling for committed annual spend. open to structuring a hybrid.
Alana (Finance): Rahul, do we have current annual committed numbers for embeddings storage?
Rahul (Procurement): Yes — last 12mo actuals: storage 18TB, egress 6TB, avg reads 120M per month. I added those to the sheet.
Priya (ML): If we reconfigure to more caching + smarter reindex scheduling we can reduce egress by ~40% on peak months. We should model both: 1) keep current infra, 2) implement caching + 6mo rollout.
Mark (Legal): If they want a 12mo commit at a discount, we need to review data deletion/export clauses and encryption-at-rest SLA. Also ask for SOC2 update and subprocessor list.
Rahul (Procurement): Proposed negotiation points: lower egress to $0.045/GB for committed tier, cap read ops for cheaper tier, 10% discount on base with 12mo commit, 60-day SLA credit multiplier for downtime. Thoughts?
Alana (Finance): Modeling that in the sheet now; 10% base discount + lower egress gets us roughly to last year's TCO assuming no growth. Put numbers in the "negotiation-options" tab.
Priya (ML): Also request a pilot: 2 months at dev tier rates for one project (Searchv2) so we can validate perf before committing. If they can supply performance histograms for p95 latency it helps the ops plan.
Sam @Procurely: We can do a 60-day pilot at dev tier rates for one namespace. We'll provide p95/p99 latency by shard and typical CPU/GPU usage.
Mark (Legal): Add standard termination for convenience at 30 days after pilot end if SLA/p95 not met for two consecutive measurement windows. We should draft that language.
Rahul (Procurement): I'll push these terms back. Alana — please confirm budget authority for committed spend up to $210k/yr if we sign the 12mo.
Alana (Finance): I can approve up to $180k/yr without exec signoff. Anything above needs CFO approval. Put the ask at $180k and ask them to meet on price.
Priya (ML): If they insist on $210k we should quantify the ops savings from reduced infra and show net benefit. I can run a quick comparison by EOD.
Rahul (Procurement): Cool. I'll send counter with: 10% base discount, egress at $0.045/GB, pilot terms, and request SOC2 cert and subprocessors. Sam — expect a note tomorrow morning.
Sam @Procurely: Sounds good. I'll prepare updated quote and SOC2 link. Thanks for the fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
FinanceBot: Monthly spend projection updated for vendors/procurely in costs dashboard.
Alana (Finance): Thanks everyone. Rahul — cc me on the counter. Priya — send the ops savings estimate when ready.
Priya (ML): Will do — pushing numbers now.
Rahul (Procurement): sending now.
Alana (Finance): marked as vendor-negotiation in the sheet + setting a follow-up check-in for next Wed 10am. :calendar:
